title: Power of Two
prompt: Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is a power of two, meaning `n` can be written as `2^x` for some non-negative integer `x`. Otherwise return `false`.
hints: You could repeatedly divide by 2 and check if you ever land exactly on 1, but there's a constant-time bit trick.
A power of two in binary has exactly one 1 bit set, and n must be positive.
For a positive n, n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit. If n is a power of two, that operation results in exactly 0, since there was only one set bit to clear.

solution.approach: A power of two has exactly one bit set in its binary representation. Clearing the lowest set bit with n & (n - 1) removes that single bit, leaving 0 if and only if n originally had just one bit set. Also require n to be strictly positive, since the bit trick alone doesn't rule out non-positive values.
